name: Progressive House
about: Progressive house is the British take on house that favoured long builds over vocal hooks. Leftfield's Not Forgotten in 1990, then Guerilla Records, Spooky and the Renaissance club in Mansfield turned trance-leaning, tribal, dubbed-out house into a form that unfolded over ten minutes rather than four. Sasha and John Digweed became its public faces, their 1994 Renaissance mix and the Global Underground series establishing the mixed CD as the genre's album format. BT, Hybrid and Way Out West added breakbeats and strings; after a dip, Deadmau5, Eric Prydz and the Anjunadeep label revived it in the late 2000s, and the Swedish big-room version of the name briefly topped the charts. At its best it is patient, melodic and built for the peak of the night.

artists.name: Sasha
artists.why: the genre's star DJ and producer

artists.name: John Digweed
artists.why: Bedrock and the Global Underground years

artists.name: Nick Warren
artists.why: Way Out West and Hope Recordings

artists.name: James Holden

albums.title: Gargantuan
albums.why: Guerilla's flagship album is progressive house before the term hardened: deep, dubby, melodic and still the scene's most underrated record.

albums.title: Dubnobasswithmyheadman
albums.why: Karl Hyde's stream-of-consciousness vocals over Rick Smith's long, pulsing builds gave the progressive era its first great band album.

albums.title: Renaissance: The Mix Collection
albums.why: The mix that invented the DJ album as art object: three discs of seamless, string-laden house that defined progressive and sold like a pop record.

albums.title: Leftism
albums.why: Dub, techno, house and Afro-beat folded into one album, with Open Up and Release the Pressure; the British dance LP against which the rest are measured.

albums.title: Ima
albums.why: Brian Transeau's debut set the trance-leaning, orchestral end of progressive house, and Embracing the Sunshine still gets played.

albums.title: Northern Exposure
albums.why: A north-and-south concept mix that moved past Renaissance into deeper, more ambient territory; many fans' favourite of their collaborations.

albums.title: Second Toughest in the Infants
albums.why: Darker and more jagged than its predecessor, with Pearls Girl and the three-part Juanita; the band's most adventurous record.

albums.title: Way Out West
albums.why: Nick Warren and Jody Wisternoff's debut brought breakbeats and Bristol atmosphere to progressive house, with The Gift as its anthem.

albums.title: Junk Science
albums.why: The Washington duo's album blends deep house, tribal rhythms and progressive builds, more songful than their mixes and better for it.

albums.title: Global Underground 006: Sydney
albums.why: Digweed's first Global Underground is the dark, driving template for the series, and the mix most often cited by his admirers.

albums.title: Global Underground 008: Brazil
albums.why: Warren's warm, melodic Brazil set is the gentler face of progressive house and the series' most sun-struck entry.

albums.title: Wide Angle
albums.why: Progressive breaks with a full orchestra and Julee Cruise on vocals; the Welsh duo's debut remains the genre's most cinematic album.

albums.title: Rhythm and Stealth
albums.why: Heavier and more hip-hop than Leftism, with Afrika Bambaataa and Roots Manuva, and Phat Planet as its bruising centrepiece.

albums.title: Global Underground 013: Ibiza
albums.why: Sasha's Ibiza set is the sound of progressive at the end of the 1990s, long, euphoric and trance-tinged, and still his best-loved mix.

albums.title: Global Underground 012: Buenos Aires
albums.why: Seaman's Buenos Aires set catches Argentina's embrace of progressive house, and his selection is tougher than his pop remixes suggest.

albums.title: Global Underground 019: Los Angeles
albums.why: Deeper and more techno-leaning than Sydney, this is Digweed's most complete mix, the point where progressive stopped sounding like trance.

albums.title: Airdrawndagger
albums.why: Sasha's only artist album trades the dancefloor for ambient, orchestral electronica and succeeds as the progressive sound's chill-out record.

albums.title: Balance 005
albums.why: Holden's two-disc mix blew progressive house open, crossing it with microhouse, electro and glitch; a scene-changing record.

albums.title: Morning Sci-Fi
albums.why: The second Hybrid album adds live drums and rock vocals to the orchestral breaks, uneven but ambitious.

albums.title: Random Album Title
albums.why: The album that brought progressive house back to the charts, with I Remember and Faxing Berlin; polished, melodic and widely imitated.

albums.title: For Lack of a Better Name
albums.why: Strobe closes the record and justifies it, a ten-minute build that became the revival's defining track.

albums.title: 1000 Words
albums.why: The Bedrock producer's second album is deep, melodic progressive house of the Digweed school, patient and precisely engineered.

albums.title: Rise
albums.why: Anjunadeep's flagship debut, soft-focus progressive house with pop vocals, and the start of the This Never Happened phone-free shows.

albums.title: Opus
albums.why: Prydz's long-delayed album is a double set of melodic progressive house at full scale, with the nine-minute title track as its monument.
